newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto to protect Roundup supply source.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto to protect Roundup supply source.

text.p: To ensure it maintains access to a key ingredient for its Roundup weed killer, Monsanto Co said it plans to rearrange its phosphorus-producing unit to accommodate a planned spin-off of its chemicals business.
"What we're going to do is set that up so both businesses will be able to have access to these materials," said a company spokeswoman, declining to discuss further details.

Monsanto's phosporus unit owns a large phosphorus mine in Idaho and supplies the raw material to various parts of the corporation that use it in production of herbicides, food products, toothpaste, cleaners and other items.
Monsanto said early Monday it plans to spin off its chemicals business into a new company. The phosphorus unit is nominally a part of the chemicals business.

The unit will be converted into a joint venture between the new company as 49-percent owner and the surviving Monsanto as 51-percent owner, according to Dain Bosworth industry analyst Bonnie Wittenburg, who said she learned about the new arrangement on a conference call with Monsanto on Monday.

"More than half of Monsanto's operating earnings are believed to come from sales of Roundup herbicide, and one of the success factors behind Roundup is its low-cost production status. The joint venture will help ensure that low-cost production status," Wittenburg said.
